issues.reason: Adorning a place is applying a decorative treatment to it, which the Patient test explicitly covers ("clean, fix, water — applying a substance or treatment changes the object"), while none of the Theme senses (acquired / transferred / moved / possessed / perceived / evaluated with no change) fits, so the unclear-case Theme default never triggers.

gaps_confirmed: no episodic/existential route for a past-tense bare-plural subject — every bare-plural verbal subject is routed to a distributing generic rule, turning an episodic report into a law

an about/depiction of-phrase on a non-deverbal noun ("posters of Saddam Hussein", the shape of the excluded "a photo of Mary"): Possession is barred and the nominalization-object rule does not apply, so no positive encoding is specified
new_gaps: the Patient/Theme object-change test never says whether decoration verbs (adorn, decorate, drape, festoon) count as "applying a treatment" — the boundary that decides this parse is left to judgment
notes: The entity-attached (Of ...) oblique is gap-territory improvisation that emits nothing false or ill-typed, so it passes the calibration line. The unfused size modifier "giant", the exposed adjectival genus on public_place and the 0.9/0.9 rule TV all follow the instruction set.
